oracle.explanation: The oracle starts a Vite dev server in middleware mode rooted at a temporary project directory containing a legitimate optimized-dependency chunk (node_modules/.vite/deps/legit-chunk.js with its own sourcemap) registered in _metadata.json. It first issues a benign request for that legitimate chunk's JS content through the transform middleware to prove normal optimized-deps serving works (operation_completed only becomes true after this succeeds). It then places a secret JSON file named unsafe.map one directory above the project root (outside server.fs.allow) and sends crafted requests reusing traversal sequences modeled directly on the optimized-deps sourcemap handler and the advisory's own fs-serve regression test (an /@fs/-prefixed path into node_modules/.vite/deps followed by '..' segments, plus a root-relative deps-prefixed variant) to reach that external unsafe.map. On patched 8.0.5, the added isOptimizedDepFile guard causes the handler to call next() instead of serving the external file, so the traversal requests fail to return the secret content, yielding exploit_succeeded=false while operation_completed remains true because the benign legitimate-chunk request already succeeded. No child processes, sockets, or files outside /tmp are used; cleanup removes the temporary directory in a finally block.
